comment: The rulings ledger. Every design decision that changes what the tool
ACCEPTS or CLAIMS gets a row here when it is made — rulings used to live
only in chat transcripts and commit messages, which is where they go to
be forgotten and re-litigated. Each ruling names the files that enforce
it; `inventory.test.js` fails if an enforcing file disappears, and
INVENTORY.md renders this ledger so the current law fits on one screen.
`open` is the other half: questions nobody has ruled on yet, each with
what would settle it. An open question that gets ruled moves UP into
decisions; it is never silently deleted.

decisions.ruling: A playthrough is a verifiable document: every catch is checked against the real encounter tables, every evolution against the real lines, every taught move against real learnsets. Undo is replay, byte-identical.
decisions.why: A box that is whatever somebody typed cannot support a nuzlocke's rules meaning anything.

decisions.ruling: A recorded fact is taken at face value: catch levels, epitaphs and teaches are the player's report of what happened in the game. The oracle refuses the impossible (wrong route, wrong level range) but never second-guesses the possible.
decisions.why: The game itself is the enforcement for what can happen; the document's job is refusing what CANNOT have happened.

decisions.ruling: Level caps are the game's own 23-row ladder from Mechanic Changes.txt, declared in the profile — never derived from the next boss's ace, which disagreed on ten rows.
decisions.why: The authored cap usually sits one below the ace, the Museum rung sits above it, and derivation invented rungs the game never lifts.

decisions.ruling: Leveling to the cap is free (the Endless Candy); every level past it spends a bagged Rare Candy.
decisions.why: That is the game's own economy, and it keeps the whole box playable without grind bookkeeping.

decisions.ruling: The dupes clause walks the game's OWN evolution graph: regional lines stay separate unless Run & Bun itself connects them (Grimer to Muk-Alola by Dusk Stone; both Basculin to Basculegion). 'forms' mode adds the regional closure on top.
decisions.why: Matches the dominant community tracker's reading, and the hack's custom evolutions are the game's statement of what a line is.

decisions.ruling: Permadeath, one-per-route, the dupes MODE and the shiny clause are independent stored toggles; --nuzlocke is only a preset. Legacy saves keep the bundle they were played under, and undo returns rules verbatim.
decisions.why: Nuzlocke tables vary rule by rule; a save silently enforcing rules the player never chose is the bug class the toggles exist to prevent.

decisions.ruling: The route rule counts LOCATIONS: a cave's floors are one encounter, and an extra method is never an extra catch (underwater grass is the route's dive method). Stored as routeUnit 'area'; pre-unit saves keep 'map' because undo replays the log.
decisions.why: Operator ruling; a replay that refuses history would brick the save.

decisions.ruling: Under the shiny clause a shiny catch is keepable over both encounter rules AND leaves the route's real random encounter owed.
decisions.why: The clause exists to never punish the 1/4096; consuming the route would.

decisions.ruling: A move whose only live routes are the egg line costs one Heart Scale at the relearner; a level-up prompt at or below the level, a TM or a tutor is free. The advisor may not offer what the bag cannot pay for.
decisions.why: Operator ruling on how Run & Bun actually serves egg moves.

decisions.ruling: Recommendation surfaces are gated by obtainability — no HM before the story hands it over, no egg move without a scale, no surfing before Surf — while the RECORDING commands stay face-value.
decisions.why: The game stops the player from doing the impossible; it does not stop a bad advisor from recommending it.

decisions.ruling: A move that faints its user is never a cell's claim while any surviving damage line exists, and a self-KO cell counts as no clean answer for us — while an enemy's sacrifice still counts as a real threat, because our death is permanent and theirs is free.
decisions.why: The optimizer sold 'teach Misty Explosion, +3 KO' to a permadeath run.

decisions.ruling: A fight with a declared permanent field (Route 119's rain, the desert's sand, Seafloor's opponent-side veil) is planned under it by default; an explicit field — even {} — is the counterfactual override, and every consumer names which sky its numbers came from.
decisions.why: A Route 119 board without its rain claims numbers the fight will never produce.

decisions.ruling: A route's opensAt is the order of the first mandatory fight standing in it, translated through name anchors — late-biased, never early. A run-map fight named after its location overrides with direct evidence. Absence means unknown, never closed.
decisions.why: For 'is this route open yet' the safe error direction is late; the source's stage headers were demonstrably stale and are ignored.

decisions.ruling: Doubles planning is opt-in ({doubles: true}) until pair lead order is sourced; double fights planned as Singles carry plannedAsSingles so the simplification is visible.
decisions.why: Measured: the lead's top action changes in 18 of 46 double fights — but which two lead is an assumption the run map cannot source.

decisions.ruling: Sibling engines are graded against shared evidence and each other, never merged: data flows with provenance, code does not. Cross-engine disagreement outside documented divergences is a red gate; documented divergences are settled by new emulator evidence, never by picking a side.
decisions.why: The differential gate caught rab's crit bug precisely because two independent engines existed.

decisions.ruling: Soul Dew is +1 SpA/SpD STAGES for the Latis (not a modifier — it composes with Calm Mind and crits ignore it like any stage), and Attract has no gender gate. Both were already implemented and pinned; the audit closed the question rather than changing code.
decisions.why: The official doc names both; Liza's Latias (Soul Dew + Calm Mind, the cap-85 rung) is where modifier-vs-stage semantics would actually diverge.

decisions.ruling: The over-cap wild catch is really a DELAYED encounter: the player saves a few choice locations for a better table later (Petalburg City held for Popplio until Surf), trading early-game tools for late-game value. Catches stay face-value — the method gates mean high-level water is unreachable until the caps have caught up anyway — and the delay itself is first-class: hold/unhold record the wait and its target, the scout stops nagging, and the routes view flips to READY when the awaited method opens.
decisions.why: Operator ruling: 'I could save routes to get those higher-value encounters later... most of the time people delay for some fairy type encounters like the Primarina line.'

decisions.ruling: An evolution is a checked event with a named price: a level evolution needs the level, a stone evolution spends the stone from the bag, a move evolution needs the move known. The advisor weighs earned evolutions as its fifth upgrade kind, judged at the projected cap like teaches.
decisions.why: The evolve command took a Ludicolo no Water Stone ever paid for, and the advisor graded level-21 Treeckos as Treeckos — which called Brawly unwinnable (0/30 rollouts) when the same box evolved won 27/30.

decisions.ruling: The run can be PLAYED here — rolls off the real tables, fights turn-by-turn against the real AI policy — but only through the same document: a roll settles as an ordinary catch or a spend (a route consumed with nothing kept), a fight ends in ordinary faint and beat commands, and the party battles at the projected cap because the infinite candy is the XP system. The battle bundle is client-held; the server keeps no fights.
decisions.why: A second, softer path into the box would fork the record: anything the recreation writes must survive the same verification a hand-reported run does.

decisions.ruling: The party ranker PLAYS its top candidates: seeded rollouts under the assignment-following floor policy, and what actually happened (wins, then deaths) outranks the grid score, which only breaks ties. pWin is a lower bound and a comparison key, never a promise; rollouts: 0 restores the grid-only answer.
decisions.why: The party ranker's grid score does not predict rollout survival: a six scoring 3.28 "all answered" (frail Tyrogue/Remoraid answers) wiped 87% of Brawly rollouts before prep, while a 0.62 six won 87%. The grid is a full-HP damage matrix — it ignores speed order and attrition. Settled by productizing the adjudication: the same tape now ranks the six that wins 12/12 above the 3.28 six that wipes.

decisions.ruling: A rolled encounter can be FOUGHT, not just clicked into the box: a 1v1 against the wild mon at its rolled level (last level-up moves it knows, Struggle if the hack gives it none), the wild side picking uniformly random moves off the seeded stream. The throw is Emerald's own capture formula (floors and all) over mainline dex catch rates, plain Poke Ball only. The ending settles the roll through ordinary commands: a caught ball is the catch, a killed encounter is the spend, a wipe records its faints and settles nothing.
decisions.why: The recreation's biggest missing risk was the catch itself — crit-kill your encounter, or lose a mon to it. Nothing here is invented: table-checked rolls, the game's formula, dex rates (PokeAPI CSV import, gated so every wild species resolves), and the same document commands every button writes.

decisions.ruling: Ball tiers are bag-backed: the plain Poke Ball stays the free baseline (always offered, never counted), while Great (1.5x) and Ultra (2x) Balls are offered only while the bag covers what the fight has thrown. Throws are counted in the battle bundle and settled into the document as `use` commands whatever the ending — the bag paid the moment they flew. `use` is acquire's other half: it refuses with the count when the bag cannot cover the claim. Run & Bun-specific ball bonuses are not modeled until someone shows the hack changes them.
decisions.why: Settles the ball-economy open question. Unlimited free Poke Balls kept the recreation playable with zero bookkeeping; making the better tiers cost bag items adds the real decision (spend the Ultra now or save it) without inventing a shop. Abandoning a fight still writes nothing, thrown balls included — the driver's nothing-until-it-ends contract outranks the cheat vector, which the honor system already owns.

decisions.ruling: Hardcore Nuzlocke: no healing or battle items in trainer fights, ever. The driver deliberately offers only moves and switches against trainers — this is the rule, not a missing feature — and the adjudicator's rollouts measure the same item-less fight the player must actually play. Balls stay legal in wild encounters (catching is what they are for), which is the only place the driver offers one.
decisions.why: Operator ruling. It also keeps the calibration honest twice over: mid-fight healing would let the recreation win fights the hardcore ruleset forbids winning that way, and the planner's damage math assumes no mid-turn potion resets on either side.

decisions.ruling: The party lead's declared ability modifies the die, exactly as the games do it: a Static lead makes half of all encounters Electric-type, Magnet Pull the same for Steel, when the method's table has any such slot (dupes still skipped). The pull reads the run's own record — no declared ability, no pull — and the roll reply names it when it fires. This is the mechanic the route strategies are built on: Granite Cave held until a Static lead exists turns Togedemaru's 5% slot into a coin flip (measured 52% over 2,000 seeded rolls).
decisions.why: Operator route knowledge, verified against the data: Route 110's all-Electric table opens at fight #48 (Camper Gavi guards it — the availability layer already knew), and the hold feature already models the delay; the pull was the missing physics. Modeled as mainline Emerald behavior until someone shows Run & Bun changes the pull rates.

decisions.ruling: Position fast-forwards: beating a fight ahead means the road behind fell on the way — that is how a run is recorded. The one way back is a DECLARED skip (`skip <trainer> [--for reason]`), the fight-side twin of `hold`: the skipped fight stays on the road (listed first among what remains), whatever it guards stays closed — a route's unlock now keys on its guard fight actually falling, not on how far the road happens to reach — and beating it later settles the skip without moving the run. The die refuses unreachable routes by naming the guard: 'Route110 is not reachable yet — Camper Gavi (#48) guards it.' AMENDED same day: most fights are REQUIRED — the road goes through them. `skip` refuses any trainer the profile does not name in `optionalFights` (curated, provenance observed; currently Camper Gavi). A skip of a required fight is a recording error, not a strategy.
decisions.why: Operator route knowledge: Camper Gavi is an optional early wall who guards the Route 110 electric grass, and the strategy of delaying him was UNREPRESENTABLE — position was monotonic, and skipping past #48 would have falsely opened the route he guards. Declared-not-implicit skips keep the fast-forward recording idiom intact for every existing run.

open.question: Is the Safari Zone one encounter or one per area? Folded to one location under the area rule; some community tables split it.
Under sun and rain the two engines disagree by exactly 1 at the low roll. The corpus has no weather observations, so neither side is ROM-verified.
open.settledBy: pykemon f4-weather-rain sweep (fixture pushed as claude/pykemon-weather-sweep-spec)

open.question: policy.SETUP remains transcription: no emulator probe has exercised the setup-move scoring the way pykemon probed SCORE_ROLL.
open.settledBy: a pykemon RAM probe over setup-move turns

open.question: Which two of a double trainer's party lead. Assumed first-two today, named as leadAssumption.
open.settledBy: emulator observation or the trainer data carrying a lead marker

open.question: Does the relearner charge a Heart Scale for a level-up move BELOW the mon's catch level (never leveled through it)? Currently free, treating candy leveling's prompts as covering everything at or below the level.

Which fights besides Camper Gavi can genuinely be walked past and returned to? The route-book survey nominates Battle Girl Luna (#162, Route 117 grass) and Picnicker Bianca (#192, Routes 111/118) as Gavi-shaped guards of optional areas; each needs in-game confirmation before joining profiles/run-and-bun optionalFights.
